checksums.formula_detail: Brute-forced sum8/sum16(LE+BE)/xor8/xor16(LE)/crc32 over 9 candidate coverage ranges (magic-only, header, records, magic+records, all-active 0x00-0x70, records-first-half, records-second-half, tail 0x60-0x70, whole 512 bytes). io_driver_functions.notes: Generic DMA3 transfer-and-wait primitive (src, dst, count|0x80000000) used by BOTH the write path (0x08049334) and the read path (0x080493f8) to pump bits through 0x0D000000. Not write-specific in practice; schema forced a single role value.

EEPROM block write: bounds-checks block address against configured max, serializes 2-bit write opcode + N address bits + 64 data bits MSB-first, kicks two DMA3 transfers via 0x080492b4. No static caller found anywhere in the 110-function decompiled set or callgraph.json.
One-line blocking wrapper: calls 0x080493f8(addr, buf, retry_forever=1). No static caller found.

EEPROM block read: sends 2-bit read opcode + address bits via 0x080492b4, then polls the EEPROM ready line at 0x0D000000 with a software timeout/retry loop. Returns 0 on success, error code on timeout.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the loader validates this literal, reload should fall back to a blank/default save; if the save still loads with save_preserved_on_load=true, the magic is not validated at boot.
Tests whether this is a hard device/format validation constant; a mismatch should either be ignored or force reinitialization of the save.

open_questions: No static caller of the EEPROM write entry point (0x08049334) or the EEPROM read entry points (0x080493e4 / 0x080493f8) exists anywhere in the 110-function decompiled trace or callgraph.json; the save-manager/serialization/checksum code that fills the 8-byte block buffers and triggers saves/loads was not captured and remains unidentified.

Checksum/integrity algorithm for header bytes 0x0C-0x0F is unknown; an exhaustive sum8/16/xor8/16/crc32 search over 9 plausible ranges on the single available .sav sample produced no match. A second differing .sav sample is required to attempt reverse-deriving a formula.

Semantic meaning of the five repeated 7-byte record patterns (offsets 0x10-0x5F) is unknown; plausible guesses (per-stage/character best-time or score entries) are unconfirmed without gameplay correlation or multiple .sav diffs.

Purpose of FUN_0804926c (branches on selector values 4 / 0x40) is unknown; it plausibly installs a save-media driver table (SRAM vs EEPROM vs Flash) but no evidence ties either value specifically to EEPROM.
Blocks 12 (0x60) and 13 (0x68) do not match the record_slotA/B pattern seen in blocks 2-11 and remain unclassified.

No paired .ss save states exist for this legacy checkpoint cohort (states/ is empty), so the mandatory pre/post save-state tracing policy could not be applied; all fuzzing_targets predictions are untested hypotheses pending a capture run that supplies paired states.

ghidra/save_related_functions.c tags 0x0804a3f0 as an MMIO-SEED, but full inspection shows it is a generic unsigned 32-bit division routine with zero hardware-register references - a false positive in the seed-selection heuristic, noted here so it is not mistaken for a save-I/O function in future passes.
